transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alicia Torres (CTO, Meridian), Ben Cho (Head of Infra), Eve Martinez (Security Eng), Samir Patel (Procurement)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Private deployment (VPC) requirements, networking (peering, endpoints), region constraints, compliance (SOC2/KMS), and rollout timeline. Agreed to follow up with technical deep dive and share security pack.

Topics: private VPC, VPC peering, interface endpoints vs private endpoints, region constraints, data residency, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML, audit logs, pilot scope, SLAs and pricing options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hi everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm jordan from redwood, i'll kick it off. 
[00:05] Alicia: hey jordan, thanks, we have a few people from infra and security on, ben, eve, samir, we'll throw questions as we go.
[00:12] Jordan: perfect, yes we wanted to understand your constraints between hosted, dedicated, and private. today looks like private vpc is front runner?
[00:20] Ben: yeah at a high level we need network isolation; can't have public endpoints for inference. so private deployment or dedicated inside our vpc via peering, something like that. also region: we run most services in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[00:34] Priya: got it. just to clarify, when you say "private" do you mean our private control plane in your VPC or fully on-prem package?
[00:41] Alicia: prefer customer-managed VPC with redwood components in our subnets, so private endpoints into our infra. on-prem is unlikely for now.
[00:49] Priya: ok good. two common patterns: (1) VPC peering to a Redwood-managed VPC with private endpoints, or (2) deployment of Redwood nodes into your VPC (private control plane where customers run the compute). both have tradeoffs.
[01:03] Ben: which one gives us the better latency / throughput?
[01:07] Priya: if you host the nodes in your VPC, latency is typically lower and you get full control over routing and egress. peering works well too but you need to manage cross-account peering limits and route table complexity. peering also means we manage the compute but traffic is private via peering and interface endpoints.
[01:23] Eve: and from a security perspective we need KMS integration and customer-supplied keys/HSM. any constraints?
[01:30] Jordan: yes we support KMS integrations, our private offering supports bringing your own KMS keys; we also have options for HSM integrations for customers with higher requirements. i'll include the exact matrix in the security pack.
[01:41] Samir: procurement question, pricing differences between dedicated reserved capacity and private vpc?
[01:46] Jordan: yes. dedicated reserved is priced as committed capacity with monthly/annual commits. private vpc where you run nodes in your account is typically license + support + infra costs (you pay the cloud infra). we'll send a side-by-side.
[01:57] Alicia: note: data residency, some clients are EU-only; we need assurance that inference data stays in eu-west-1 for european tenants.
[02:06] Priya: we can pin model variants and routing policies by region. for private deployment you control the region. for peered managed vpc we can designate eu-only pools and route european traffic there.
[02:17] Ben: regarding network, do you use interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) or NAT traversal?
[02:22] Priya: we typically recommend interface endpoints / PrivateLink for API ingress; for control-plane telemetry we use private peering and VPC endpoints. NAT is avoided in most enterprise setups to keep traffic internal.
[02:33] Ben: any limits around peering connections per account? we've run into limits before, multiple peering sessions per environment get messy.
[02:38] Priya: yeah peering scales but has complexity; we often recommend Transit Gateway for larger fleets. we can support both, transit gateway, VPC peering, and also VPC endpoints. depends on your infra design.
[02:50] Eve: audit logs, we need to retain request/response logs for 90 days and have them sent to our central logging. how does that work with private?
[02:57] Jordan: the private deployment can push audit logs to your s3/elk stack via private endpoints. for managed peered deployments we can stream logs over private link to your account. retention is configurable. we'll include exact log types in the pack (request ids, prompt hashes, metadata, we avoid storing sensitive data unless configured).
[03:16] Alicia: about model versions, we need to freeze a version for compliance. can we pin to a specific model and prevent auto-upgrades?
[03:23] Priya: yes, pinning supported. rollouts can be canary / manual. auto-upgrades only happen if you opt in.
[03:29] Ben: network egress, if we bring nodes into our VPC do you still need any outbound to redwood control plane?
[03:36] Priya: minimal. For private control plane deployments we still have a control plane handshake for control plane telemetry, but you can opt for an air-gapped mode where control plane is fully in your VPC and Redwood's control plane is not reachable. that becomes more of an on-prem scenario.
[03:51] Samir: procurement: SLA expectations, what uptime do you guarantee for private vpc?
[03:56] Jordan: dedicated / private enterprise packages include an SLA we can negotiate. hosted tier has standard SLA. i'll send the SLA doc; enterprise private deployments typically have higher guaranteed uptime tied to runbook and on-call commitments.
[04:08] [05:00-ish silence as docs are shared]
[04:11] Alicia: we have a couple technical follow-ups, 1) exact CIDR ranges needed for endpoints, 2) do you support cross-region failover for models, 3) how do you handle KV cache and state if we run multiple zones?
[04:22] Priya: for CIDR we can accept either a small set of interface endpoint IP ranges or you can open a peering block. we'll provide a template. cross-region failover is supported via model routing policies and autoscaling across pools; but cold start and KV warm-up are considerations. KV cache is per-pool; if you run multiple zones we either replicate cache or accept warm-up on failover, we can design around that.
[04:43] Ben: replication of KV for low latency is important for us, can we replicate across regions?
[04:47] Priya: we have a replication pattern for critical state, but it's an advanced config. typically customers accept regional isolation for lowest latency and route traffic to nearest region. replication adds complexity and cost.
[04:58] Eve: compliance: SOC2 report, ISO, penetration test results, can you share?
[05:03] Jordan: yes we'll share our latest SOC2 and the redacted pentest summary. for private you also get audit hooks and can run your own scans.
[05:11] Alicia: SSO, we use Okta, need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[05:15] Priya: supported, SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC available. for API keys we support rotation and scoped keys.
[05:24] [06:00, short discussion about timeline]
[05:27] Alicia: timeline wise, we'd like a pilot in 6-8 weeks, vendor selected by end of month.
[05:32] Jordan: that timeline is realistic; pilot can be a 2-4 week evaluation with restricted workloads and can include performance benchmarks.
[05:39] Ben: benchmarks, we need to run latency tests against our typical prompt distribution, can your team run the benchmark on our infra?
[05:45] Priya: yes we can run benchmarks. usually we run a small harness in your environment with sample prompts and measure p99 latency, throughput, and token cost. we'll need network access and test data (sanitized).
[05:56] Samir: procurement again, what's the process for signing up, do you need an MSA?
[06:00] Jordan: for enterprise private we do an MSA; we'll share sample MSA + security addendum.
[06:06] Alicia: couple of specifics on endpoints: do you support AWS PrivateLink for the API and do you need route tables modified?
[06:13] Priya: yes PrivateLink is our recommended approach for API ingress; you create an interface endpoint on your side and we approve the endpoint. route tables typically don't need wide changes. we'll provide a step-by-step template.
[06:24] Ben: any IAM role assumptions for the nodes if we deploy them into our account?
[06:28] Priya: nodes require ecs/ec2/iam roles depending on deployment. we provide a minimal set of IAM policies required for the compute to run and for KMS access. we'll provide terraform modules to speed up provisioning.
[06:39] Eve: data in transit, do you support mTLS between your services and our infra?
[06:44] Priya: yes mTLS is supported end-to-end, and TLS 1.2+ by default. for higher assurance we can enable client certs and mutual auth.
[06:53] Jordan: ok we're at about 40 minutes, want to summarize next steps?
[06:57] Alicia: yes please.
[07:00] Jordan: recap: jordan will send security pack (SOC2, pentest summary), architecture templates (cidr, endpoint templates), and pricing comparison (dedicated vs private). priya will schedule a technical deep dive / network workshop week of 2026-04-13. meridian will share VPC diagram and preferred region (ben). procurement (samir) will confirm timeline and any PO processes.
[07:18] Ben: will send VPC info by friday.
[07:20] Samir: procurement will circle back with contract questions after we review MSA.
[07:24] Eve: i'll compile the compliance questions, expecting the security pack early next week.
[07:28] Jordan: great. i'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the docs. thanks everyone.
[07:33] Alicia: thanks team bye.

Attachments/links referenced: Security pack (link), Private deployment architecture template (link), Pricing comparison spreadsheet (link)

End of transcript.
